'''Robert Wayne Alexander''' (March 19, 1941 {{ndash}} January 6, 2023) was an American biologist and cardiologist known for research in the fields of [[atherosclerosis]], hypertension, and vascular biology.<ref name="wileyonl">{{cite journal |title=Robert Wayne Alexander |journal=Clinical Cardiology|volume=30|issue=11|pages=581–582|doi=10.1002/clc.20133 |pmid=18000973|year=2007 |last1=Hurst |first1=J. Willis |doi-access=free |pmc=6652906 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Robert Wayne Alexander was born on March 19, 1941, in Memphis, Tennessee.<ref name="wileyonl"/>  

After he graduated high school, Alexander was accepted to the [[University of Mississippi]] where he graduated in 1962. Alexander then attended classes at [[Emory University]] While at Emory, Alexander was a regular at the Emory faculty's Saturday Morning Clinical [[Cardiology]] at [[Grady Memorial Hospital]]. In 1967 he obtained from Emory University his M.S Degree and a year later he obtained his Ph.D.<ref name="wileyonl" /> Upon graduation from Emory, Alexander attended [[Duke University School of Medicine]], graduated in 1969, and then began an internship under James Wyngaarden. He would return to Duke in the mid-1970s to complete his cardiology fellowship as a member of the [[United States Public Health Service]].  Alexander took up residency at the [[University of Washington School of Medicine]] which he completed a few years later.<ref name="wileyonl" />

==Career==
Alexander was the Senior Surgeon at the Experimental Therapeutics Branch of the National Heart and Lung Institute until 1976 when he became a [[Harvard Medical School]] faculty member at the [[Brigham and Women's Hospital|Peter Bent Brigham Hospital]]. In 1982, he became an Associate Professor of Medicine at Harvard. In 1988, he became the R. Bruce Logue Professor of Medicine and Director of the Division of Cardiology at Emory University in Atlanta where he attended years before.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brad Berk on gut-instinct, decisions |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/rochester-magazine/mind-body-soul/2016/03/11/brad-berk-what-i-know/80860064/ |website=Rochester Democrat and Chronicle |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref> He kept all of the college's faculty and he brought in new researchers. Five years later Alexander co-founded Atherogenics Inc. and he served as its director and board member until 2009.<ref name="blmg44">{{cite web |title=R. Wayne Alexander M.D Ph.D. Executive Profile & Biography |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=526062&privcapId=269643731 |website=Bloomberg |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref> Alexander became [[Emory University School of Medicine]] Chair in 1999.<ref name="wileyonl"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Physicians' group studies liver treatments, drugs - |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/stories/1999/11/15/newscolumn2.html |website=Biz Journals (Atlanta Business Chronicle) |date=15 November 1999 |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref> In 2013, Alexander stepped down as Emory University's department of medicine chairman but he stayed on with the department of cardiology in a faculty role.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anti-aging tricks from dietary supplement seen in mice |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2015/08/150821111051.htm |website=Science Daily |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref>

==Research==
Alexander began his research while he studied for his Ph.D. at Emory University. He published over 250 scientific publications<ref name="wileyonl"/> and provided edits for ten books. Alexander has contributed notably to the vascular biology field of study taking it from basic observations to applications that could be applied clinically, including drug development.<ref name="wileyonl"/> The editors at [[Hurst's the Heart]] selected Alexander as one of the people to contribute to the textbook. Alexander directly has supervised twenty-five postdoctoral fellows. An award at Emory University Atlanta (R. Wayne Alexander Excellence in Research Accomplishment Award) is named after Alexander.<ref>{{cite web |title=Congratulations to our 2016 Faculty Award winners |url=http://www.emorydailypulse.com/2016/06/22/congratulations-2016-faculty-award-winners/ |website=Emory Daily Pulse |access-date=17 November 2018|date=2016-06-22 }}</ref> Alexander has been a part of organizations such as the [[American Heart Association]]. He's been on the editorial board of various journals.<ref name="wileyonl"/>

===Controversy===
In the early 2010s, six of the papers that belonged to Alexander's research group were retracted.<ref name="forbes17">{{cite web |title=3 More Retractions For Emory Cardiology Group |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/larryhusten/2013/12/26/3-more-retractions-for-emory-cardiology-group/ |work=Forbes |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref> Co-author Lian Zuo was blamed for the first of three retracted papers but not for the newer ones which were retracted for image manipulation.<ref name="forbes17"/> The newer retracted published papers were from the early-mid 2000s and were in the Journal of Biological Chemistry, in circulation (one paper), and on Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis, and Vascular Biology (two papers).<ref name="crbef">{{cite web |title=Scientific Fraud Found In Wayne Alexander's Research Group At Emory |url=http://www.cardiobrief.org/2011/04/27/scientific-fraud-found-in-wayne-alexanders-research-group-at-emory/ |website=Cardio Brief |access-date=17 November 2018|date=2011-04-27 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1971, Alexander married Jane Mansfield Woods and they had three children together.<ref name="wileyonl"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Elizabeth Caudell and David Alexander |url=https://thebrunswicknews.com/announcements/engagements/elizabeth-caudell-and-david-alexander/article_e0a1eee9-8c46-579b-88db-02bfa1281274.html |website=Brunswick News |access-date=17 November 2018}}</ref> Alexander died on January 6, 2023, due to neurodegenerative disease.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander, Robert Wayne |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/obituaries/alexander-robert-wayne/D3ZZXWO5PBD7NH4NIQR2EJ54D4/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=February 10, 2023 |language=English}}</ref>
